subject: Performance MAP: quantization + kernel profiling plan and initial results
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-10T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Performance MAP kickoff — quantization + kernel profiling

Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to capture the MAP milestones and a concrete performance evaluation plan so your engineering team can validate latency/throughput and quality tradeoffs before finalizing the purchase. Attached is a draft MAP (acme_map_v1.pdf) and a short initial results CSV from a smoke run (bench_results_initial.csv).

High-level ask: please confirm the target SLOs below and the acceptance gates so our teams can schedule runs on your preferred hardware next week. If agreed, we’ll treat this plan as the performance milestone in the MAP and run the formal harness on 11/12–11/14.

Target SLOs (proposed)
- p50 latency (prompt+generation): <= 120ms for 128-token high-tps workload
- p95 latency: <= 320ms at target concurrency
- Throughput: >= 3000 tokens/sec (sustained) for the batch/continuous-batched workload
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): <= 40ms for cold requests
- Concurrency: validate at 1, 8, 32 concurrent streams

Quantization/Kernels to test
- Baselines: FP16 and BF16 (reference)
- Quantized variants: INT8 (dynamic/static), INT4 experimental (per-layer calibration)
- Kernel profiles: fused_matmul, fused_attention, kv_cache-copy, softmax-approx
- Compare kernel latency breakdown and GPU utilization per run

Acceptance / regression gates
- Output-quality: embedding cosine >= 0.985 vs FP16 baseline on the eval set; top-token match >= 97% (sampling normalized)
- Perf-regression: quantized variant p95 increase <= 5% vs FP16; throughput drop <= 10%
- No functional regressions on our prompt-suite (sanity-pass for generation safety checks)

Next steps
1) Please confirm the hardware you want us to run (we can provision A100/H100/T4) and any access constraints.
2) Confirm the acceptance gates or propose edits.
3) Agree target contract signature timeline — we suggested 2025-11-22 in the MAP draft.

Attached: acme_map_v1.pdf, bench_results_initial.csv

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side before we sign off:
1) For INT4, is the plan to do per-layer calibration or post-training quantization? We want to understand retraining needs.
2) What exactly will your regression check compute for "top-token match" — is that strict equality or tolerance-aware?
3) Can you provide an explicit schedule of when you’ll deliver the kernel profile outputs and the consolidated MAP artifact?

Also, procurement needs a clear timeline — legal will want the MAP and performance appendix by 11/17 to meet our finance sign-off on 11/24. Can you meet that?

Jordan
Director of AI Engineering — Acme Robotics
jordan@acme.ai

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-12T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Performance MAP kickoff — quantization + kernel profiling

Jordan — thanks, answers inline and schedule below.

1) INT4 approach
- We will run both per-layer calibration (preferred, higher accuracy) and a fast PTQ-style post-training path. Per-layer calibration will require sample calibration data (we included a 5k-sample subset in the MAP drive link). We will document any fine-tuning requirement; plan assumes no retraining for the initial MAP but we’ll surface delta-quality if retraining is beneficial.

2) Top-token match definition
- For deterministic prompts we compute exact top-token match. For non-deterministic sampling prompts we compute top-k overlap (k=3) with temperature-normalized resampling. We will report both strict and tolerance-aware metrics; the acceptance gate uses the tolerance-aware metric unless you prefer otherwise.

3) Delivery schedule (tentative)
- 2025-11-12: run harness on A100 (reference) + H100 spot checks; deliver kernel_profiles_20251112.zip and bench_results_initial.csv (smoke results included).
- 2025-11-13: completed INT8 runs and initial INT4 per-layer calibration; upload raw logs and CSVs.
- 2025-11-14: consolidate results and run regression checks using the eval harness; produce MAP performance appendix (acme_map_v1_performance.pdf).
- 2025-11-17: deliver final MAP + acceptance appendix for procurement/legal (if no last-minute re-runs).

Bench plan details (short)
- Workloads: 1) continuos low-latency single-stream; 2) high-concurrency chat simulation (8/32 streams); 3) throughput-batched generation (large batch sizes for embedding-heavy flows)
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, TTFT, tokens/sec, GPU SM utilization, memory footprint, kernel-level timing (ms per-kernel per-token)
- Regression checks: automated eval harness applies prompt-suite of 450 pairs (accuracy + safety + hallucination tests) and computes embedding cosines, top-token overlap, and BLEU/ROUGE for retrieval+generate flows
- Hardware: primary reference A100-80GB; optional H100 for 1:1 comparison; T4 for cost-optimized profile

Acceptance gates (concrete numbers)
- Embedding cosine >= 0.985 (FP16 baseline) for INT8; >= 0.98 for INT4 (experimental)
- Top-token tolerance-aware >= 96% for INT8; >= 92% for INT4
- p95 latency regression <= 5% INT8; <= 12% INT4 (experimental cap)

We can meet 11/17 delivery for the MAP appendix if we run the scheduled tests this week and there are no unexpected failures. I’ll schedule cluster time today. Please send the calibration sample set to rishi@redwood.ai and confirm the hardware preference (A100 + H100 spot).

Attachments to be uploaded: kernel_profiles_20251112.zip, bench_results_initial.csv, eval_harness_config.yaml

Thanks —
Rishi

Two quick operational notes from the MAP/CS side:
- We’ll attach the consolidated eval runbook to the MAP appendix (eval_harness_config.yaml). That runbook includes the exact prompts, sampling seeds for reproducibility, and the automated regression pass/fail script.
- If INT4 shows regressions beyond the experimental caps, our standard fallback in the MAP is to recommend INT8 + kernel-level micro-optimizations (we have a short list of kernels to tune; see kernel_profiles_20251112.zip).

Close timeline:
- As Rishi noted, our target signature date in the MAP is 2025-11-22. To make that work we need a clean performance appendix by 2025-11-17 and any legal redlines by 11/19 EOB. Procurement at Acme indicated finance approval on 11/24, so that aligns if we keep to the schedule.

Operational ask from Acme
- Please confirm: (a) acceptance gates above, (b) hardware: A100 + H100 spot, (c) that legal receives performance appendix by 11/17.

I’ll coordinate the CS handoff and set a brief 30-minute review on 11/18 to walk the MAP appendix if needed.
